questions.q: Moment of inertia of a square plate of side l about the axis passing through one of the corner and perpendicular to the plane of square plate is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Use parallel axis theorem to get the magnitude of the moment of inertia of a square plate of side l about the axis passing through one of the corners and perpendicular to the plane of a square plate, 

Iz=Icm+Ml22

⇒Iz=Ml26+Ml22=4Ml26=2Ml23.

questions.q: A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg , kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque about bottom point
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{F} \times 2 \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{I} \alpha \\ & 49 \times 2 \mathrm{r}=\frac{7}{5} \mathrm{mr}^2 \alpha \\ & 14=4 \mathrm{r} \alpha
\end{aligned}$
As sphere rolls without slipping
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{r} \alpha \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{14}{4}=\frac{7}{2}=3.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2
\end{aligned}$

In order to produce a rotational kinetic energy of <math><mn>1200</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the angular acceleration of <math><mn>20</mn><mi> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></math> must be applied about the axis for a duration of:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that, 

Rotational kinetic energy, K=12Iω2 

⇒12Iω2=1200
⇒12×1.5×ω2=1200
⇒ω=40 rad s-1

We also know that, ω=αt
⇒t=4020=2 s

questions.q: A thin circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with angular velocity $\omega$. If another disc of same dimensions but of mass $\mathrm{M} / 2$ is placed gently on the first disc co-axially, then the new angular velocity of the system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_1 \omega=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2} \omega=\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}\right) \omega_2 \\ & \omega_2=\frac{2}{3} \omega\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A solid cylinder and a solid sphere, having same mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>, roll down the same inclined plane from top without slipping. They start from rest. The ratio of velocity of the solid cylinder to that of the solid sphere, with which they reach the ground, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
During pure rolling, the work done by the friction is zero. Therefore, we can apply conservation of mechanical energy.

mgh=12mv2+12IvR2

⇒mgh=12m+IR2v2

⇒v=2gh1+ImR2

For a solid cylinder ImR2=12 and for a solid sphere, ImR2=25

vCylvSph=1+251+12=1415

questions.q: a string is wound around a hollow cylinder of mass $5 \mathrm{~kg}$ and radius $0.5 \mathrm{~m}$. If the string is now pulled with a horizontal force of $40 \mathrm{~N}$, and the cylinder is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface (see figure), then the angular acceleration of the cylinder will be (Neglect the mass and thickness of the string)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: From newton's second law $40+\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{R} \alpha)$ ...(i) Taking torque about 0 we get $40 \times \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{f} \times \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{I} \alpha40 \times \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{f} \times \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{mR}^{2} \alpha40-\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{mR} \alpha$ ...(ii) Solving equation (i) and (ii) $\alpha=\frac{40}{\mathrm{mR}}=16 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$

questions.q: A thin circular ring of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is rotating with a constant angular velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in a horizontal plane about an axis vertical to its plane and passing through the center of the ring. If two objects each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> be attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of ring, the ring will then rotate with an angular velocity (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the masses are gently placed we can apply conservation of angular momentum.

Initial moment of Inertia I1=MR2

Final moment of inertia I2=MR2+2mR2

By conservation of angular momentum

I1ω1=I2ω2⇒MR2×2=M+2mR2×ω2

⇒ω2=2MM+2m rad s-1

ℓ=4.4ly=4.4×9.46×1015

length of Arc. =ℓ=Rθ

θ=4 S=4×4.843×10-6=1.94×10-5 rad

questions.q: If a solid sphere of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and a disc of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> have the same radius, then the ratio of moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane to the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about any diameter is given by, 2m1R25.

Using parallel axis theorem, we get

Isolid sphere =25m1R2+m1R2=75m1R2

=75×5R2

=7R2

Moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is given by, m2R24.

Now using parallel axis theorem, we get

Idisc =m2R24+m2R2=54m2R2

=54×4R2

=5R2

Therefore,Idisc Isoild sphere =57

Thus, x=5.

questions.q: A ring and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of both bodies are identical and the ratio of their kinetic energies is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In pure rolling work done by friction is zero. Hence, potential energy is converted into kinetic energy. Since initially the ring and the sphere have same potential energy, finally they will have same kinetic energy too.
∴ Ratio of kinetic energies =1
⇒7x=1⇒x=7
